verdict: THE METABOLIC HALF IS SOLVABLE PER CONDITION, BUT NOT UNIQUELY, AND THAT DISTINCTION IS THE ANSWER. Human-GEM has 12,931 reactions of which 5,725 are reversible -- no curated ordering exists for any of them, because in metabolism direction is a consequence of flux rather than an annotation. Running FBA and reading sign(v) off a single optimum would give a direction for every one of them, and would be misleading: the optimum is unique in its objective value and essentially never unique in its flux distribution, so that sign is an arbitrary vertex of a large alternate-optima space. MEASURED with flux variability analysis at 90% of optimum, which asks whether the sign is forced rather than merely observed: 2,280/5,725 (39.8%) of reversible reactions have a DETERMINED direction, 2,851 (49.8%) are genuinely UNDETERMINED, and 594 carry no flux at all. So the answer to 'can we solve it for any condition we like' is: yes, every condition yields a self-consistent answer -- but the answer is a consequence of the objective and uptake bounds you chose, both of which are assumptions rather than measurements, and for a substantial minority of reactions the optimum does not pin the direction down at all.
